"Create a complete, playable top-down 2D browser game called \"Mr. Rescue: Extinguish Protocol\". Use HTML5 Canvas + vanilla JavaScript (single HTML file preferred, or clean multi-file if needed). Pixel-art style inspired by the original Mr. Rescue: chunky 16–32px tiles, limited palette, firefighter character with red helmet/visor and yellow suit, furniture, ladders/stairs, windows, and fire effects.

CORE CONCEPT
Translate the original Mr. Rescue (side-view multi-floor building rescue) into a strict top-down view. Player controls the firefighter. Primary goal is still rescuing civilians, not just extinguishing everything. The game must feel fast, tense, and challenging.

ORIGINAL MECHANICS TO PRESERVE / TRANSLATE
- Rescue civilians by interacting with them (pick up / escort) and bringing them to windows, exits, or safe zones. In top-down this becomes carrying them (slower movement) or guiding them to an exit.
- Heat management: Suit heat rises near fire or when hit by enemies. Collect coolant items to reduce heat. Full heat = death.
- Resource management: Extinguishers have limited capacity / ammo that recharges slowly or via pickups. Overuse is punished.
- Fire spreads over time if left unchecked (especially on furniture and floors).
- Power-ups: Coolants, extinguisher refills/expansions, heat resistance, temporary speed, etc.
- Score system based on civilians saved, enemies defeated, time, and combos.
- Multi-floor / multi-room buildings. Progress by clearing civilians on a floor then reaching the stairs/elevator to the next.
- Procedural or semi-procedural room layouts with obstacles (tables, sofas, walls, debris).

NEW REQUIRED SYSTEMS (critical)
1. Four extinguisher types the player must switch between (hotkeys 1–4 or mouse wheel + number keys):
   - Water (blue) – effective only against standard/wood/charcoal fires
   - CO2 (white/gray) – effective only against gas/electrical/phantom fires
   - Chemical / Foam (yellow-green) – effective only against magma/oil/chemical fires
   - Ice (light blue) – effective only against frostfire / unique cold-fire enemies (or freezes certain hazards)

2. Four distinct moving fire enemy types. Each is ONLY vulnerable to one specific extinguisher. Wrong extinguisher does nothing or slightly worsens the situation (spreads, enrages, or applies a debuff).
   Suggested mapping:
   - Charcoal Crawlers / Ember Sprites → Water
   - Gas Phantoms / Leak Ghosts → CO2
   - Magma Brutes / Oil Blobs → Chemical
   - Frostfire Sprites → Ice

   Enemies must actively move: patrol routes, chase the player or civilians, spread fire, or attack. Some can block paths.

3. Puzzle-like mechanics mixed with action:
   - Path-blocking fires that require the correct extinguisher to clear.
   - Sequence puzzles (extinguish A then B to open a door or stop a gas leak).
   - Environmental interactions: Ice freezes a moving platform or locks a door; Water cools an overheating mechanism; CO2 disables electrical barriers; Chemical dissolves debris.
   - Civilians in danger that require the right extinguisher nearby before you can safely rescue them.
   - Limited extinguisher charges force planning and prioritization.
   - Rooms with mixed enemy types that punish spamming one extinguisher.

GAMEPLAY REQUIREMENTS
- Top-down camera (fixed or slight follow). Tile-based or free movement with collision.
- Player movement: WASD or arrows. Aim with mouse or secondary stick. Fire extinguisher with mouse click or space (stream that lasts while held, consumes ammo).
- Switch extinguishers instantly with 1–4 keys. Show clear UI indicator of current extinguisher + remaining ammo for all four.
- Civilians: Wander or hide. Player can pick up (carry) or interact to send them toward the nearest exit. If they touch fire or an enemy for too long, they die (penalty + possible fail condition if too many die).
- Heat bar and individual extinguisher ammo bars always visible.
- Fire spreads from enemy contact or over time on flammable tiles.
- Challenging difficulty: Enemies are aggressive, fire spreads, ammo is limited, heat rises fast, and wrong extinguisher wastes precious resources. Include a few difficulty options or scaling.
- Multiple levels/floors with increasing complexity, mixed enemy types, and puzzle rooms. End of floor requires all (or most) civilians rescued.
- Simple menu, restart, and high-score / best-rescues tracking (localStorage).

TECHNICAL @COMMENT_BODY@ POLISH
- Clean, readable code with comments. Use requestAnimationFrame game loop.
- Collision detection, simple AI for enemies (state machine: patrol → chase → attack), particle effects for extinguishers and fire.
- Pixel-art friendly rendering (imageSmoothingEnabled = false).
- Sound effect placeholders (or simple Web Audio beeps) for extinguishing, pickup, death, rescue.
- Responsive enough for desktop; keyboard + mouse focused.
- Include a short in-game tutorial or first room that teaches switching extinguishers and matching types.

VISUAL STYLE
Match the original Mr. Rescue vibe as closely as possible in top-down form: dark building interiors, wooden floors, pinkish or beige walls, furniture (sofa, tables, clock, windows), ladder/stairs, and the firefighter character. Fires should have distinct visual differences per type so the player can quickly identify which extinguisher is needed.

Deliver a fully working game. Prioritize fun, clear feedback, and the extinguisher-matching + puzzle tension over perfect art. Start with 3–5 solid rooms/floors that demonstrate all systems.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

Usage: playwright-cli <command> [args] [options]
Usage: playwright-cli -s=<session> <command> [args] [options]

Core:
  open [url]                  open the browser
  attach [name]               attach to a running playwright browser
  close                       close the browser
  detach                      detach from an attached browser
  goto <url>                  navigate to a url
  type <text>                 type text into editable element
  click <target> [button]     perform click on a web page
  dblclick <target> [button]  perform double click on a web page
  fill <target> <text>        fill text into editable element
  drag <startTarget> <endTarget> perform drag and drop between two elements
  drop <target>               drop files or data onto an element
  hover <target>              hover over element on page
  select <target> <val>       select an option in a dropdown
  upload <files...>           upload one or multiple files
  check <target>              check a checkbox or radio button
  uncheck <target>            uncheck a checkbox or radio button
  snapshot [target]           capture page snapshot to obtain element ref
  find [text]                 search the page snapshot for text or a regexp, returning matching nodes with surrounding context (like search snippets)
  eval <func> [target]        evaluate javascript expression on page or element
  dialog-accept [prompt]      accept a dialog
  dialog-dismiss              dismiss a dialog
  resize <w> <h>              resize the browser window
  delete-data                 delete session data

Navigation:
  go-back                     go back to the previous page
  go-forward                  go forward to the next page
  reload                      reload the current page

Keyboard:
  press <key>                 press a key on the keyboard, `a`, `arrowleft`
  keydown <key>               press a key down on the keyboard
  keyup <key>                 press a key up on the keyboard

Mouse:
  mousemove <x> <y>           move mouse to a given position
  mousedown [button]          press mouse down
  mouseup [button]            press mouse up
  mousewheel <dx> <dy>        scroll mouse wheel

Save as:
  screenshot [target]         screenshot of the current page or element

Tabs:

  tab-new [url]               create a new tab
  tab-close [index]           close a browser tab
  tab-select <index>          select a browser tab

Storage:
  state-load <filename>       loads browser storage (authentication) state from a file
  state-save [filename]       saves the current storage (authentication) state to a file
  cookie-list                 list all cookies (optionally filtered by domain/path)
  cookie-get <name>           get a specific cookie by name
  cookie-set <name> <value>   set a cookie with optional flags
  cookie-delete <name>        delete a specific cookie
  cookie-clear                clear all cookies
  localstorage-list           list all localstorage key-value pairs

  localstorage-set <key> <value> set a localstorage item

  unroute [pattern]           remove routes matching a pattern (or all routes)
  network-state-set <state>   set the browser network state to online or offline

DevTools:
  console [min-level]         list console messages
  run-code [code]             run playwright code snippet

  video-start [filename]      start video recording
  video-stop                  stop video recording

  video-hide-actions          stop annotating actions performed on the page
  show                        show playwright dashboard
  pause-at <location>         run the test up to a specific location and pause there
  resume                      resume the test execution
  step-over                   step over the next call in the test

  highlight [target]          show (or with --hide, remove) a highlight overlay for an element; `--hide` without a target hides all page highlights.

Install:
